extracted.intended_audience: school and university administrators, Title IX Coordinators, compliance officers, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements that K-12 and postsecondary institutions must follow when responding to reports of sexual harassment under Title IX, including reporting channels, ‘‘actual knowledge’’ triggers, supportive measures, grievance options, training, remedies, and anti-retaliation protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient accountability to restore or preserve equal access
rubrics_metrics.description: When sexual harassment constitutes sex discrimination covered by Title IX, the final regulations hold schools accountable for responding in ways that restore or preserve a complainant's equal access to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains that supportive measures and remedies required by the final regulations are designed to restore or preserve equal access. The regulations prescribe specific recipient actions when sex discrimination takes the form of sexual harassment so complainants are not faced with institutional betrayal or a non-supportive response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures irrespective of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to complainants irrespective of whether the complainant files a formal complaint that initiates a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.44(a) specifically requires the Title IX Coordinator to contact the complainant to discuss supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes with respect to supportive measures, and explain the option for filing a formal complaint. Supportive measures are intended to restore or preserve equal access to education and may be provided even when no formal complaint is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide remedies when respondent found responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a respondent is found responsible for sexual harassment as defined in §106.30, the recipient must provide remedies to the complainant designed to restore or preserve the complainant's equal access to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations expressly require the Title IX Coordinator to be responsible for the effective implementation of remedies (§106.45(b)(7)(iv)). Remedies must be meaningful and aimed at restoring equal access; recipients are expected to implement them effectively and promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, accessible reporting channels (any person may report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may report sexual harassment (whether or not the person reporting is the person alleged to be the victim) using the contact information listed for the Title IX Coordinator or by any other means that results in the Title IX Coordinator receiving the person's verbal or written report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.8 requires the Title IX Coordinator contact information to include an office address, telephone number, and email address; reports may be made at any time, including during non-business hours, by using the telephone number or email address or by mailing to the office address. The Department aims to give complainants and third parties clear reporting channels and predictability about recipient response obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘‘Actual knowledge’’ trigger for elementary and secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: In elementary and secondary schools, notice of sexual harassment to any employee constitutes actual knowledge to the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.30 defines 'actual knowledge' to provide that notice to any elementary and secondary school employee triggers the recipient's response obligations; 'notice' includes but is not limited to reporting to the Title IX Coordinator as described in §106.8. This contrasts with postsecondary procedures where students retain more autonomy over disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiated autonomy for postsecondary students
rubrics_metrics.description: In postsecondary institutions, students retain more autonomy and control over deciding whether, when, or to whom to disclose a sexual harassment experience without automatically triggering a report to the Title IX office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations preserve more decision-making agency for postsecondary students regarding disclosure and reporting, while still ensuring recipients meet response obligations when there is actual knowledge under applicable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX personnel impartiality and freedom from conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Title IX Coordinator must be free from conflicts of interest and bias and Title IX personnel must be trained to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment of the facts at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires training for Title IX personnel on how to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment. The Department emphasizes that no recipient may apply harmful stereotypes or prejudge complainants based on personal characteristics or identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit retaliation against individuals exercising Title IX rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations prohibit retaliation against any individual exercising Title IX rights, including the right to refuse to participate in a grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added §106.71 to expressly prohibit retaliation. This protection covers complainants, respondents, and any person involved in the process and is enforced vigorously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not ignore reports; must provide prompt, meaningful responses
rubrics_metrics.description: No recipient is permitted to ignore a sexual harassment report, regardless of the identity of the person alleged to have been victimized, and complainants may expect prompt, meaningful responses from their schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations present a consistent, predictable framework for when and how a recipient must respond to Title IX sexual harassment; reporting may be hard for complainants, so recipients' responses should be timely, substantive, and not dismissive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer voluntary informal resolution processes as alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may choose to offer informal resolution processes as alternatives to a full investigation and adjudication of the formal complaint, with the voluntary consent of both the complainant and respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes that informal resolution options may encourage some complainants to file a formal complaint where they might otherwise be reluctant to do so if only full investigation and adjudication were available. Informal resolution is voluntary for both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator contact duties and information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must contact the complainant to discuss supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes, explain the option for filing a formal complaint, and the Coordinator's contact information must include address, telephone, and email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions to §106.8 and §106.44(a) codify these duties and contact-information requirements; reports may be made at any time, including outside business hours, to ensure accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and mitigation of stereotypes that deter reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure Title IX personnel are trained to avoid biases and stereotypes (including race- and sex-based stereotypes) that may lead to ignoring, blaming, or punishing certain complainants and thereby deter reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes historically marginalized communities are often more likely to be disbelieved or punished; requiring impartial training and prohibiting prejudgment aims to reduce institutional betrayal and barriers to reporting.
